RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is not evidence of bias. For a "head of" position, banks frequently prioritize regulatory credibility and stakeholder management over pure quantitative depth, making the chosen candidate's background highly relevant. 

Raising sex discrimination without concrete evidence—such as biased remarks or demonstrable procedural irregularities—lacks legal merit and risks damaging your professional reputation in a specialized market. Delays in HR feedback are common and not indicative of wrongdoing. 

Instead of questioning the panel's composition, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback focused on skills or leadership competencies you can develop for future executive roles.
